entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Khālid ibn ʿAbd al‐Malik al‐Marwarrūdhī was a 9th-century Baghdadi astronomer of Persian descent, born in the city of Marw, in what is now western Afghanistan, to a family of scholars.


He spent his life studying and teaching astronomy in Baghdad, producing works that were influential in the development of Islamic astronomy and its transmission to Europe during the Middle Ages.


Khālid ibn ʿAbd al‐Malik al‐Marwarrūdhī's contributions to astronomy include his cataloging of celestial bodies and his work on the calculation of planetary orbits.


His legacy can be seen in the work of later astronomers, such as Al-Biruni, who built upon Khālid's discoveries and made significant contributions to the field of astronomy.


A striking testament to Khālid's enduring impact on the history of astronomy is the presence of his works in the manuscript collections of the Umm al-Khayr library in Baghdad, which date back to the 13th century.

entities.summary:
Khālid ibn ʿAbd al‐Malik al‐Marwarrūdhī was a 9th-century Baghdadi astronomer who made significant contributions to the field of astronomy during the Islamic Golden Age. His most notable work, the “Al-Zij al-Marwarrudhi’, was a comprehensive astronomical table that accurately predicted celestial bodies and eclipses. This work was widely used and respected by scholars across the Middle East and North Africa, showcasing the importance of Arabic astronomy during this period.

Khālid ibn ʿAbd al‐Malik al‐Marwarrūdhī was born in 900 CE in Baghdad, Iraq, and died under unknown circumstances. His work as an astronomer had a lasting impact on the development of astronomy in the Islamic world, influencing later scholars such as Al-Biruni and Ibn Yunus. The legacy of his work can still be seen in modern astronomical tables and calculations.

In the context of the Islamic Golden Age, Khālid ibn ʿAbd al‐Malik al‐Marwarrūdhī was a key figure in the pursuit of knowledge and scientific advancement. His contributions to astronomy demonstrate the importance of interdisciplinary approaches to scientific inquiry and the value of cross-cultural exchange in the development of human knowledge.
